title: Three DATETIME columns hold local time, and the other 31 hold UTC
summary: MySQL triggers write local time into 3 columns, and the service writes UTC into the other 31. Convert all 34 columns to timestamptz, each read in its true time zone.

blocks.title: The problem
blocks.html: A MySQL DATETIME value has no time zone. The value means UTC or local time, depending on the code that wrote it. The copy to PostgreSQL must know which.

blocks.title: What we found
blocks.html:
• [READ] The service sets its clock to UTC. 31 of the 34 DATETIME columns get their values from the service. [src: report.md]
  • [READ] 3 columns get their values from MySQL triggers that call NOW(). The host runs on local time (UTC+1, with daylight saving). [src: report.md]
  • [TESTED] For the same order, order_events.created_at is 1 or 2 hours later than orders.created_at. [src: report.md]
  • [INFERRED] At each autumn clock change, one local hour occurs two times. About 38,000 rows fall in these hours. [src: report.md]

blocks.title: Why it matters
blocks.html: Reports that join these tables show times that are 1–2 hours wrong. If the copy reads all 34 columns as UTC, the error becomes permanent in PostgreSQL.

blocks.title: Proposed action
blocks.html: Convert all 34 columns to timestamptz. Read each column in its true time zone. Mark the ambiguous rows in a new column tz_ambiguous. In PostgreSQL, the triggers call now(), which returns a timestamptz. New rows are then correct. Effort: 3 days.

options.label: Convert all 34 columns to timestamptz, each in its true zone
options.detail_html: Effort: 3 days. The times become correct in all reports. About 38,000 old rows keep a flag, because their true time is ambiguous.

options.label: Copy the values as timestamp without time zone
options.detail_html: Effort: half a day. The copy is simpler. The mixed time zones stay, and the reports stay wrong by 1–2 hours.

recommendation_html: Option a. The move is the cheapest time to fix the data. After the move, each fix needs a new migration of a 288 GB table.
